html:
The Oghuz were a western branch of the Turkic peoples, nomads who in the 700s formed a confederation on the steppes between the Aral Sea, the Syr Darya and the Caspian. The map shows a wide Oghuz area around 900.

Their rulers, the yabgus, had their winter town at Yangikent on the lower Syr Darya. They traded with the Samanid cities to the south, fought the Khazars and pushed the Pechenegs west. Ibn Fadlan met them in 922 on his journey to the Volga.

Oghuz who took up Islam became known as Turkmen. One Oghuz clan, the Seljuks, moved south in the 1000s and founded the Seljuk Empire, which opened Anatolia to Turkish settlement. The Turks of Turkey, the Azerbaijanis and the people of Turkmenistan all descend in large part from the Oghuz. See also the Oghuz on the map.
